terra.problem: The proverb describes how people respond under two conditions; it does not say they are the same individuals in both cases.
The verse does not connect the man who loves wisdom with guarding wealth.
Squandering wealth does not necessarily mean it runs out. The verse does not say that it does.
Calling a net a different kind of planting muddles the comparison. A net is spread, not planted.
The explanation repeats the answer and contrast without adding a distinctive voice or insight.
Having no regard for the cause of the poor does not necessarily mean the wicked never give it a thought.
The verse says the wicked have no regard for these concerns, not that the concerns never register with them.
The verse says the wise turn away anger; it does not explicitly say they calm the city down.
No resolution does not establish that there is no ruling or that the wise man still has to deal with the fool.
The verse says what happens if a ruler listens to lies. It does not say officials follow whatever their ruler listens to.
Neither the righteous who flourish in verse 2 nor the wicked who thrive in verse 16 are called rulers in those verses.
The explanation simply repeats both halves of the verse and the answer, without a distinctive voice or further insight.
The proverb says the servant understands but will not respond. It does not say whether he remembers the words.
The explanation points to the words at the end of the verse but adds only a restatement, with no meaningful insight or distinctive voice.
The verse says the servant will bring grief; it does not say that grief is waiting for him.
The explanation repeats the verse's contrast without adding insight or a distinctive voice.
The explanation restates both halves of the verse without adding insight or a distinctive voice.
The verse says many seek the ruler's favor; it does not describe a crowd chasing the ruler.
The proverb describes mutual detestation, but it does not say whether the people involved ever end up as friends.
The verse says the upright person is detestable to the wicked. It does not say they know exactly what they think of him.
